classification.difficultyReason: Differentiate a supplied cubic volume function, distinguish an interior stationary point from a boundary point and compare endpoint volumes.

content.prompt:
A box is made by cutting out square corners from a rectangular piece of cardboard.

The volume in $\mathrm{cm}^3$ depends on the side length $x$ of the squares that are cut out.

The volume formula is given by
$$V(x)=x(12-2x)^2$$
where $0\le x\le6$.

Find the side length of the squares that maximises the volume of the box, and the maximum volume.

spec.sourceRegion: Right side of the second practice question
spec.description: Unshaded schematic open-box net with a horizontal central rectangle and four flaps. The outer boundary is solid, the four central fold lines are dashed, and x labels the upper-left flap depth. Proportions are schematic.
spec.mathematics: Four square corners have been removed. The flap depth is x; no other dimensions are printed.
spec.answerVisibility: Only supplied outline, fold lines and x label are visible.

answer.worked:
$$\begin{align*}V(x)&=144x-48x^2+4x^3\\V'(x)&=144-96x+12x^2\\0&=12(x-2)(x-6)\\x&=2\text{ or }6.\end{align*}$$
The interior stationary point is at $x=2$; $x=6$ is an endpoint.
$$\begin{align*}V''(x)&=24x-96\\V''(2)&=-48<0.\end{align*}$$
Thus $x=2$ gives a local maximum. Compare its volume with the endpoint volumes:
$$\begin{align*}V(2)&=2(12-4)^2\\V(2)&=128\\V(0)&=0\\V(6)&=0.\end{align*}$$
Cutting out squares of side length $2\ \mathrm{cm}$ gives the maximum volume of $128\ \mathrm{cm}^3$.
